title: client-rotation-429-timeline-scratchpad
content:
Quick purpose: personal timeline + commands I ran while chasing a recurring 429 pattern that coincided with client-id rotation (new keys issued every 6h by the integration).

High-level summary:
- Observed: Several customers reported bursts of 429s starting ~2025-02-10 14:10 UTC. 401s accompanied some requests for a short window.
- Hypothesis: Our key rotation + short TTL on quota caches causes transient quota mis-attribution; SDK retries + aggressive backoff may make it worse.
- Immediate mitigation tried: pushed a hotfix to SDK to fall back to client-id header when Authorization missing, and temporarily increased per-key soft quota in the proxy for affected customers.

Timeline / breadcrumbs (local times shown in UTC):
- 2025-02-10 13:58 — Customer support thread: "generation failing with 429" (tickets: RED-9483). Attachment from customer: curl snippet and raw headers.
- 2025-02-10 14:10 — First spike in infra metrics: per-key 429 rate for key prefix abc123 jumped from ~0.2% to 6% for 20 minutes.
- 2025-02-10 14:12 — I asked for raw gateway logs (edge-nginx) for that key window. Got log slice: see sample below.
- 2025-02-10 14:15 — Noted overlapping rotation event in key-service: keys with client-id abc123 were rotated 14:11–14:13.
- 2025-02-10 14:20 — Reproduced locally by simulating rapid key swap + concurrent requests from multiple clients.
- 2025-02-10 14:45 — Rolled proxy rule to tolerate missing auth header for 2m during rotation (hotfix). 429s fell back to baseline by ~14:50.

Commands and snippets I ran while reproducing locally:
- Basic curl that reproduces a 401 when auth header dropped:
  curl -i -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACED" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

  (Response sampled)
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  Date: Mon, 10 Feb 2025 14:08:21 GMT
  Content-Type: application/json
  Content-Length: 92

  {"error":{"message":"invalid api key","type":"authentication_error","code":"invalid_api_key"}}

- Curl when quota header present and 429 returned:
  curl -i -X POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACED" \
    -H "X-Client-Id: abc123" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"hello again"}' \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

  (Response sampled)
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Date: Mon, 10 Feb 2025 14:11:34 GMT
  Content-Type: application/json
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
  Retry-After: 60

  {"error":{"message":"rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit_error","code":"quota_exceeded"}}

- Edge logs (nginx-like) extracted for abc123 window (anonymized):
  2025-02-10T14:11:12Z 10.12.15.200 "POST /v1/generate" 200 312 "-" "SDK/py v1.3.0" client_id=abc123 keyhash=sha256:REDACTED quota_remain=1
  2025-02-10T14:11:33Z 10.12.15.201 "POST /v1/generate" 429 128 "-" "SDK/py v1.3.0" client_id=abc123 keyhash=sha256:NEWKEY quota_remain=0
  2025-02-10T14:11:34Z 10.12.15.202 "POST /v1/generate" 429 128 "-" "SDK/py v1.3.0" client_id=abc123 keyhash=sha256:NEWKEY quota_remain=0
  2025-02-10T14:11:36Z 10.12.15.203 "POST /v1/generate" 401 92  "-" "SDK/py v1.3.0" client_id=abc123 keyhash=sha256:NEWKEY

Observations & notes:
- The keyhash in logs flips from OLDKEY to NEWKEY during the 14:11–14:13 window. Some requests during the flip show quota_remain=1 then 0 then missing.
- SDK/py v1.3.0 in user agents for these requests — our known SDK that does token refresh via background thread. If token rotate + request race occurs, Authorization header can be momentarily omitted (we've seen similar in older SDK).
- X-RateLimit headers are set by the quota-proxy; when the key-service returns a "not found" for a brief interval during rotation, quota-proxy classifies as no-quota and returns 429.
- Retry-After is present and usually set to 60s for soft-limits. Client SDK retries after backoff, leading to request bursts as many in-flight retries align after Retry-After expires.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Rotation TTL race: Key-service marks old key revoked and new key active but cache invalidation timing for quota-proxy is lagging -> transient not-found -> 429. (LIKELY)
2) SDK bug: background refresh removes Authorization header for a split second while swapping token in memory -> gateway sees missing Bearer and responds 401 which then the client tries to re-auth and replays, causing quota attribution weirdness. (LIKELY for 401s seen)
3) Rate-limit accounting sharding: Quota proxy shards by keyhash; rotation causes some requests to appear under a different shard which has zero remaining quota while other shard still has remaining tokens. (POSSIBLE)
4) Client-side retry fanout: aggressive exponential backoff with low jitter results in retry bunching. (POSSIBLE)

Quick experiments to validate hypotheses (results):
- Disabled key rotation for a small subset (canary customer) for 24h — no 429 spikes during that window. (Supports hypothesis 1)
- Introduced additional logging in SDK to print when Authorization header is cleared vs set — reproduction run showed a 120ms window where header was not present on an in-flight thread. (Supports hypothesis 2)
- Forced quota-proxy cache TTL to 30s (was 5s) and replayed rotation: 429s reduced but not eliminated (mitigates, but doesn't fully fix). (Partial support for hypothesis 1/3)

Mitigations and next steps (owned items):
- Short term (hotfixes):
  - Proxy: tolerate temporary key not-found for 10s if recent rotation event detected (rolled 2025-02-10 14:45) — reduces 429 blowups. (owner: Alex)
  - SDK: quick patch to avoid dropping Authorization during background refresh and add jitter to retry timing (PR linked). (owner: Priya)
- Medium term:
  - Key-service: emit explicit "rotation-in-progress" signal to quota-proxy so it can avoid hard 429s (ticket RED-9483, ETA 2w). (owner: Maya)
  - Quota accounting: make quota attribution atomic across rotation boundary (design doc needed). (owner: infra team)
- Long term:
  - Consider per-client warm-up quota transfer for new key so rotation doesn't create zero-balance windows.

Notes for postmortem checklist:
- Capture rotation timeline automatically on future incidents (correlate key-manager events with edge logs).
- Add metric for Authorization-header-absent spikes per client during rotation windows.
- Add test in SDK e2e to simulate rotation while in-flight requests exist.

Random debugging commands / queries I used (for future reference):
- kibana query for keyhash: 
  @timestamp:["2025-02-10T14:10:00" TO "2025-02-10T14:20:00"] AND client_id:abc123 | sort @timestamp asc
- postgres: check key rotations: 
  SELECT client_id, old_key_hash, new_key_hash, rotated_at FROM key_rotations WHERE client_id='abc123' AND rotated_at > '2025-02-10' ORDER BY rotated_at DESC;
- small python snippet to hammer with varying jitter (used to reproduce):
  import requests, time, random
  for i in range(200):
      time.sleep(random.uniform(0,0.05))
      r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REPLACED','X-Client-Id':'abc123'}, json={'input':'x'*10})
      print(i, r.status_code, r.headers.get('Retry-After'))

Questions I still have / need help with:
- Does the quota proxy have a local in-memory cache that could be made consistent across multiple instances during rotation? (ping infra)
- Can key-service provide an "expected-activation-time" in the rotation API so we can schedule a rolling-safe window? (ping key-service)
- Is there an easy way to instrument SDKs in customer fleets to send a one-off diagnostic header during rotation so we can measure header-drop prevalence without full shipping?

If I forget: main takeaways = rotation + cache TTL + SDK header swap = brief window of 401/429 spikes. Hotfixes mitigated; need design changes to make rotation atomic from quota viewpoint.

TODOs (personal):
- Draft short postmortem note (2–3 paragraphs) once logs aggregated.
- Write design doc for quota atomicity approach.
- Coordinate with support for proactive messaging to customers with automatic key rotation enabled.

-- Maya
